REVIEWER: Please move `BASE_FEATURE_SECTION` on `__ELF__` to `.data.rel.ro..cr_features` (with the matching `link_section` update in `base/feature.rs`). Now that the descriptor is immutable, the explicit `.data..cr_features` attribute is what keeps it in writable `.data`: without it, a `constinit const Feature` holding two pointers is placed in `.data.rel.ro` and ends up in `GNU_RELRO`, read-only after relocation and shared across forked processes on Android/Linux/ChromeOS, matching the read-only placement this CL achieves on Windows. SuperSize still classifies it as a feature: `MapFileParserLld` strips the `.data.rel.ro` output-section prefix before `_FlagsFromMangledName()` checks for `.cr_features` (`tools/binary_size/libsupersize/linker_map_parser.py`).

```cpp
#if defined(__ELF__)
#define BASE_FEATURE_SECTION \
  __attribute__((section(".data.rel.ro..cr_features")))
#else
#define BASE_FEATURE_SECTION
#endif
```

REVIEWER: This is a very big performance hit for the software encoding. Now there will be an additional roundtrip to the GPU process to make a readback.

I think it's still possible to premap here.

The d3d11_shared_image_buffer_tracker still holds the dxgi_handle (used to copy the camera texture in DeliverTextureToClient). So you can make it also hold a SharedMemoryRegion and populate it with data on `DuplicateAsUnsafeRegion()`.

The only question is how to pass it through the mojo.

The [ExportedSharedImage](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:gpu/ipc/common/exported_shared_image.mojom;l=29;drc=3ffedad30b40ca5332cfd1cd02ace6c918c18243) still has `buffer_handle`, which contains native_handle, which [contains](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:ui/gfx/mojom/native_handle_types.mojom;l=87;drc=55c26cfa56aece65a1f69f7da6d85e67710a3fd6) shmem region for windows.

Then on the receiver side, the ClientSharedImage already [can be](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:gpu/command_buffer/client/client_shared_image.h;l=207;drc=0b303deec2fd0684d76593143445a48923cafbf9) created with a sharedmemory mapping.

Maybe a cleaner solution would be to add a new SharedMemoryRegion to mojo ExportedSharedImage and change the ClientSharedImage to hold the ShMemRegion instead of a Mapping.

It will require some changes to actually populate that field and read it on the receive side, but I don't see fundamental obstacles on implementing it.
OWNER: Thanks — that's a fair point, and the premap handling is now addressed on PS10. The slot tracker (`D3D11SharedImageBufferTracker`) holds a shared-memory region populated on demand in `DuplicateAsUnsafeRegion()`, and the region is delivered alongside the exported shared image in `SharedImageBufferHandleSet`. The renderer's software-fallback path maps that region and wraps the frame directly, mirroring the GMB path — so software-only consumers no longer need a GPU readback to read shared-image frames.

I went with the region field on the capture-side handle struct rather than a field on `ExportedSharedImage` because `MappableBufferDXGI::CloneHandle()` doesn't carry the region today and its import path drops it, so the region would not survive an `Export/ImportUnowned` roundtrip. When the MappableSI conversion lands, the region can move into the exported image's buffer_handle and this capture-side field can be folded away.

We shall file a follow up bug (maybe that already exists?) for "Convert MediaFoundation video capture to MappableSI" that will: (1) have MappableBufferDXGI::CreateFromHandle retain the region and make `SetUsePreMappedMemory(true)` serve it from `Map()/MapAsync()` i
REVIEWER: The bug is crbug.com/404905709, but it's more general, not only about video capture on windows.

Meanwhile there might be something missing on the VideoCaptureImpl side or mojom traits. How does the premapped region end up inside the ClientSharedImage?
OWNER: Today it doesn't — the region rides as a separate field on `SharedImageBufferHandleSet` because `MappableBufferDXGI` drops the handle's region at import (see its region_ comment). The path once the MappableSI conversion lands (crbug.com/404905709):

1. `MappableBufferDXGI::CreateFromHandle` retains the region from the DXGI handle;
2. the tracker exports the slot image with buffer_handle (`Export(/*with_buffer_handle=*/true`)), which carries the region via `CloneWithRegion; ClientSharedImage(ExportedSharedImage)` already calls `CreateMappableBufferFromHandle`, so the imported image ends up holding a `MappableBufferDXGI` with the region — no new import plumbing needed;
3. `SetUsePreMappedMemory(true)` (exists but dormant) makes `Map()/MapAsync()` serve that region instead of the readback path.
REVIEWER: I don't think this is what's happening. There's no shared memory region populated inside the GMB handle. In the capturer you populate a separate region, which is sent as a new `premapped_region` in the `SharedImageBufferHandleSet`. It's not a part of dxgi handle struct. That one has a shared region, but it's not populated. I don't see where the new `premapped_region` is used in the ClientSharedImage.

OWNER: Done in PS13 - the region now travels inside the shared image, and the separate `premapped_region` field on `SharedImageBufferHandleSet` is gone.

How the region ends up inside the `ClientSharedImage`:

1. `D3D11SharedImageBufferTracker::Init()` allocates the region, attaches it to the slot's DXGI handle (`CloneWithRegion`), and imports the texture through the buffer-usage `CreateSharedImage` overload, so the capture-side `ClientSharedImage` keeps a `MappableBuffer` around the handle.
2. `DuplicateAsUnsafeRegion()` fills that region on every premapped frame (it is the same shared memory the handle's region refers to).
3. `GetVideoBufferHandle()` exports with `Export(with_buffer_handle=true)`; `MappableBufferDXGI::CloneHandle()` clones the DXGI handle including its region, so the region rides in `ExportedSharedImage.buffer_handle`. The mojom side needed nothing new - the DXGI handle's `shared_memory_handle` field already serializes it.
4. In the renderer, `ClientSharedImage::ImportUnowned()` constructs the image from the exported handle; the `ClientSharedImage(ExportedSharedImage)` constructor runs `CreateMappableBufferFromHandle()`, and `MappableBufferDXGI` retains the DXGI handle

REVIEWER: **jonross** we should likely exit early here. If the `RHWV*` was deleted, that would be triggered by the `WebContents` being destroyed. The test being added misses this by only deleting the view.

If `InitAsChild` pumps a nested message loop that "tears the tab down" (as described in the commit message), then `WebContentsViewAura` (`this`) and `render_widget_host` are also likely destroyed during that loop.

Operating on `this` after `InitAsChild` returns is a Use-After-Free (UAF). Specifically, calling `GetRenderWidgetHostViewParent()` on line 1087 or passing `this` to `SetDragDropDelegate` on line 1094 will crash if `this` has been deleted.

The browser test masks this issue because it only calls `Destroy()` on the view, leaving `this` and `render_widget_host` alive. To properly fix this, you likely need a way to track if `this` or the `WebContents` survived the nested message loop, and return early if they did not.

REVIEWER: Just checking the intended lifetime here.

Once an origin has a grant, `GetPermissionStatus()` returns `GRANTED`, so `PermissionContextBase::RequestPermission()` returns early and never reaches
`DecidePermission()`. The embedder's `permissionrequest` handler then isn't checked again for that origin until the guest is destroyed.

If that matches clipboard and is what we want, that's fine. Otherwise, should grants be cleared on cross-document navigation?
OWNER: Yes, this intentionally mirrors clipboard permissions: grants are scoped to the `WebViewGuest` lifetime and the requesting origin.

In `<webview>`, embedders frequently navigate inside the guest or run single-page apps (such as Google Meet or Zoom) where permissions are expected to persist for that origin for the duration of the guest session without re-prompting the embedder on subsequent requests. Navigating to a different origin still requires a separate grant.

If we want finer-grained per-document scoping in the future, we could explore clearing on cross-document navigation in a follow-up, but matching clipboard's guest-lifetime origin-scoped semantics is the desired behavior for now.

REVIEWER: I think dtor will touch multiple cache-lines if the object is large. Do you think it matters here?
OWNER: It matters: reading every cache line before freeing roughly halves the quarantine's overhead on storms (e.g. storm_1k_cold: +75.4% [74.8, 76.3] -> +28.9% [28.0, 29.2] for browser_main, 50 runs, 95% CIs). Zapping misses the CPU cache on lines that weren't read, and is cheaper on lines that were.

Our informed guess (not measured) of what destructors read: most lines of class instances (vptr and fields with non-trivial destructors, e.g. pointers, strings, containers, callbacks), all lines of arrays of such objects, and nothing of byte or trivially destructible buffers (e.g. string characters, `std::vector<uint8_t>`, pixels). So real destructors are likely between the two variants, depending on the mix of object types.

Added an `_all_lines` variant of each scenario, so the results bound real destructors from both sides. Results are in the CL description.

The spec condition is:

```
  dpb_size >= sps_max_dec_pic_buffering_minus1 + 1 - TwoVersionsOfCurrDecPicFlag

For streams accepted by this parser, `TwoVersionsOfCurrDecPicFlag` is 0 because

  dpb_size > sps_max_dec_pic_buffering_minus1
```

pre-store DPB size is at most `sps_max_dec_pic_buffering_minus1`, then
`StorePicture(curr_pic_)` can bring the DPB up to the allowed
